original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The categories $\text{Simp}(\mathcal{A})$ and
$\text{CoSimp}(\mathcal{A})$ are abelian.
\item A morphism of (co)simplicial objects
$f : A \to B$ is injective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is injective.
\item A morphism of (co)simplicial objects
$f : A \to B$ is surjective
if and only if each $f_n : A_n \to B_n$ is surjective.
\item A sequence of (co)simplicial objects
$$
A \xrightarrow{f} B \xrightarrow{g} C
$$
is exact at $B$ if and only if each sequence
$$
A_i \xrightarrow{f_i} B_i \xrightarrow{g_i} C_i
$$
is exact at $B_i$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let A be an abelian category.
conclusions: Simp(A) and CoSimp(A) are abelian categories.
For every morphism f of (co)simplicial objects, f is mono if and only if each f_n is mono.
For every morphism f of (co)simplicial objects, f is epi if and only if each f_n is epi.
A sequence of (co)simplicial objects A→B→C is exact at B if and only if its component sequence is exact at B_n for every n.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extension}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$ and
let $k$ be an integer $\geq 0$. Consider the
simplicial object $E$ defined by the following rules
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E_n = \bigoplus_\alpha A$, where the
sum is over $\alpha : [n] \to [k + 1]$ whose
image is either $[k]$ or $[k + 1]$.
\item Given $\varphi : [m] \to [n]$ the map
$E_n \to E_m$ maps the summand corresponding
to $\alpha$ via $\text{id}_A$ to the summand
corresponding to $\alpha \circ \varphi$,
provided $\Im(\alpha \circ \varphi)$
is equal to $[k]$ or $[k + 1]$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to K(A, k) \to E \to K(A, k + 1) \to 0
$$
which is term by term split exact.
hold_reason: The pinned lemma directly follows a definition of the Eilenberg–Mac Lane object K(A,k)=i_{k!}U using a particular explicitly described truncated simplicial object U. The proposed standalone formula defines E but never defines K(A,k) or K(A,k+1), leaving its exact sequence between undefined source-specific objects.
proposed_correction: Expand the source's construction of K(A,k) as the Eilenberg–Mac Lane object of A in degree k (via the prescribed truncated simplicial object and left Kan extension), and similarly for k+1; retain exact sequence with degreewise splitting and independently review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-abelian-limit-skeleta}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
For any simplicial object $V$ of $\mathcal{A}$ we have
$$
V = \colim_n i_{n!}\text{sk}_n V
$$
where all the transition maps are injections.
